title: Italy Rewrites Its Electoral Rules While Bracing for a Fiscal Reckoning · 20 Oct
keywords: Italy, electoral reform, majority bonus, Giorgia Meloni, fiscal policy, deficit, debt, defense spending, energy inflation, EU fiscal rules, euro area, Italian politics, 2027 budget, trade unions, diesel prices, coalition politics, constitutional reform
notes: Italy's parliament has approved a sweeping electoral reform that grants majority bonus seats to any alliance crossing 42% of the vote, raising questions about democratic fairness and political engineering. Simultaneously, Rome faces a worsening fiscal outlook, with the deficit projected to climb to around 3.4–3.5% of GDP in 2027, driven by rising defense commitments, energy costs, and debt-servicing burdens. Together, the two developments capture Italy's central tension: a government seeking firmer political control at the very moment economic constraints are narrowing its room to deliver.
